text:
tony: :rotating_light: alert — reserved-gpu pool 'resv-enterprise-1' reporting 100% allocation, queue length increasing. Autoscaler showing repeated failures to provision new nodes. Impacting a small set of enterprise tenants (corp-enterprise, zenhealth). I’m paging oncall.

oncall-bot: @tony — PagerDuty incident created: PD-46812 — Reserved pool saturation. Incident channel: #incidents. Escalation: oncall -> infra.

miguel: I’m on it. Just checked the autoscaler logs, seeing repeated rate-limited API errors to cloud provider when creating instances: `QuotaExceeded` followed by backoff retries.

sasha: Confirmed queues for reserved pool have ~120 pending sessions, avg wait ~45s, tail latency spiking. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/cluster/resv-enterprise-1 (link)

carol: Customer-ops pinged: corp-enterprise reports degraded response times and some requests hitting 429. They’re on standby in the bridge.

customer-ops: corp-enterprise: "we're seeing timeouts for our background jobs and some live requests failing. Can you confirm this is on your end?"

tony: Replying to them: yes, reserved pool exhausted, working on mitigation. Will provide ETA in 10m.

miguel: Root cause sketch: autoscaler requests are being throttled by provider due to burst quota cap. autoscaler keeps backing off, so pool doesn't expand and scheduler leaves pods pending. Also one heavy tenant (zenhealth) has several long-running priority jobs causing noisy-neighbor effects.

niraj: Suggest immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily increase autoscaler parallelism/replace with a manual API push to provision a small number of nodes (if quota allows), 2) evict lowest-priority sessions in reserved pool, 3) move best-effort tenants to shared pool fallback.

sasha: Agreed. I can run an eviction script to free up ~10 GPUs from low-priority sessions. Need approval to evict non-enterprise best-effort jobs.

tony: Approved. Execute eviction and start migration plan for best-effort tenants. Miguel — can you attempt a manual node create with reduced parallelism? We need to avoid more quota errors.

miguel: Running manual create with 2 nodes at a time and 5s spacing. Command:```bash
# manual node create (cloud cli)
cloudctl compute instances create --type g4dn.xlarge --count 2 --label resv-enterprise-1 --region us-west-2
sleep 5
cloudctl compute instances create --type g4dn.xlarge --count 2 --label resv-enterprise-1 --region us-west-2
```

infra-bot: autoscaler: create_instance call returned 429 -> quotaExceeded. Attempt 1/5. Backoff 10s.

miguel: Second batch also hit quota limit. Provider quota still limiting — we can either request emergency quota bump (takes ~30–60m) or steal capacity from shared pool.

sasha: Eviction script ran: evicted 12 best-effort sessions (non-SLA) from resv-enterprise-1, freed 6 GPUs. Scheduler placed some pending high-priority pods on freed GPUs, tail latency improved slightly.

tony: Good. Start redirecting new best-effort allocations to shared pool using temporary routing policy. Who can flip the routing rule?

niraj: I’ll patch routing policy for resv-enterprise-1 to deny best-effort classes and re-route to shared-fallback for 30m. Patch snippet:```json
{"route":{"match":"tenant.class==best-effort","target":"shared-fallback"}}
```Applying now.

infra-bot: routing-policy: patched for resv-enterprise-1 — best-effort -> shared-fallback.

carol: Notifying customers: corp-enterprise and zenhealth informed that we performed prioritized evictions and temporary routing. corp-enterprise acknowledged and asks for ETA to full resolution.

customer-ops: corp-enterprise: "Thanks for the update. Can you guarantee no more evictions of our sessions?"

ton y: Replying: We're not evicting corp-enterprise. Evictions targeted best-effort only. Continuing to work on capacity.

miguel: Next step: schedule a maintenance increase for the reserved pool quota with cloud provider; submitting emergency ticket now with justification (customer-impacting enterprise tenants). Ticket ID: CLOUD-TKT-9921. ETA unknown.

sasha: Queue length dropped from 120 -> 42 after evictions + routing. Latency normalized for corp-enterprise mostly, but zenhealth still has 15 long-running sessions taking a lot of GPU memory.

niraj: For zenhealth noisy sessions, propose soft-evict + restart to reclaim memory: run `kubectl drain --grace-period=30 --ignore-daemonsets` targeting their pods with low-priority flag, then reschedule on shared nodes.

miguel: I can coordinate with dev on zenhealth. Recommending running node-level restart with `preemptible=true` to force eviction and reschedule. Will only target non-enterprise pods.

tony: Keep me posted. If CLOUD-TKT resolves quickly we’ll scale; otherwise we keep the routing and evictions until next patch. Also open question: why autoscaler didn't failover to other regions? We had cross-region fallback enabled.

niraj: Autoscaler attempted cross-region but prefers same AZ for reserved pools; fallback requires manual override. We can manually spin up a couple of instances in us-east-1 as temporary measure but need to ensure routing allows cross-region placement for reserved tenants.

miguel: I can enable cross-region fallback for this pool temporarily. Patch command:```bash
redwoodctl pools update resv-enterprise-1 --fallback-region us-east-1 --enable-temporary-fallback true
```Applying now.

infra-bot: pool update accepted. Cross-region fallback enabled for 60m window.

sasha: New nodes registered in us-east-1 show up as available. Scheduler placed 8 pending tasks across regions, pending queue down to 19. Observability shows request 429s dropping.

carol: corp-enterprise thanks the team on the bridge. They asked for a postmortem and mitigation plan to prevent noisy neighbor causing enterprise impact.

tony: Action items: 1) follow up CLOUD-TKT-9921 until quota bump or permission to provision, 2) schedule post-incident noisy-neighbor policy (priority shaping + eviction thresholds), 3) create runbook for manual cross-region fallback and emergency node provisioning, 4) temporary increase observability alert thresholds to reduce noise. Assigning: miguel (1), niraj (2,3), sasha (4).

miguel: I’ll own the ticket and update every 15m. First update in 15.

oncall-bot: Incident PD-46812 status: acknowledged -> mitigation in progress. Next update scheduled at +15m.

tony: Thanks everyone. Stand down for now but remain available; keep this thread for comms.

carol: Will draft customer-facing timeline and postmortem skeleton.

sasha: Adding logs and flamegraphs to the incident doc. Also saving autoscaler traces for root cause analysis.

miguel: CLOUD-TKT-9921 updated: provider responded requesting additional justification and temporary quota increase approved for +8 GPUs in us-west-2 — will be available in ~7 minutes.

infra-bot: cloud: quota increased, new nodes provisioning allowed. Autoscaler resumed normal create flow.

sasha: Pool utilization down to 84% now, pending queue 6, no further 429s observed. Marking immediate mitigation as successful.

tony: Closing incident when metrics stable for 30m. Please add any follow-ups to the incident board. Thanks all.
